title: Meet Australia
description: Travel to Australia with Spark and Mango: a country in Oceania whose capital is Canberra, where people speak English and pay with the Australian dollar — plus two places we'd love to visit.

body.heading: Where in the world is Australia?
paragraphs: Australia is a country in Oceania, the island region of the south-west Pacific. Australia is so big that it is both a country and a continent — the smallest continent in the world.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Australia is Canberra. Canberra was built on purpose as the capital, so that Sydney and Melbourne would not have to argue about which of them should win!

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in Australia is English.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Australia is the Australian dollar.

body.heading: How big is Australia?
paragraphs: Australia covers about 7,692,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. It is the largest country in Oceania.

body.heading: A fact to wow your friends
paragraphs: The Great Barrier Reef is the world’s largest coral reef system. It is the largest living structure on the planet — so big that it is made of billions of tiny coral animals working together.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth — families snorkel from reef pontoons with turtles, clownfish and coral gardens in warm water.
Uluru rises from the desert at the heart of Australia — sacred to the Anangu people, it changes colour from ochre to glowing red at sunset.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Australia on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: Australia in one breath: a country in Oceania, capital Canberra, where people speak English and pay with the Australian dollar.
materials: A globe, atlas or world map (to find Australia)
Paper and crayons or pencils for the screen-free mission
supervision: Read this one together: a grown-up can help with tricky place names and hunt for Australia on the map as you read.
safetyNotes: Reading only — no physical activity is involved.
If your family ever visits the watery places in this article, water fun in Australia always needs a grown-up watching closely.
